text:
oliver: Heads-up: I sketched a small follow-up to the dashboard rendering RFC. idea: split panel render into prefetch (authn/authz + data fanout) and render-worker (pure rendering + layout). goal is to dedupe RBAC checks and let the render path be extremely hot and cacheable.

maya: sounds promising. what's the main perf win we expect?

oliver: rough numbers: RBAC checks currently add ~15-30ms per panel call and are repeated for N subrequests. if we prefilter at the prefetch stage and return a signed token (short-lived, per-request) to render workers, we avoid repeated checks and reduce tail latency.

sam: how do you see token shape? opaque vs signed jwt? replay/forgery concerns?

oliver: thinking opaque session-like token referencing a prefetch result in a sharded cache (small TTL). metadata: tenant, allowed-entities, policy-version, checksum. render-workers validate the token against cache+checksum. no downstream policy evaluation.

jen: TL;DR authz move to edge microservice, then render becomes stateless and fast. what's the fallback when prefetch misses?

oliver: fallback flows: 1) prefetch miss -> synchronous prefetch (adds latency) 2) degrade to old flow (render worker runs authz) for canary traffic 3) respond with partial content + placeholder. plan is conservative canary first.

kevin: big question: what about multi-panel coalescing? dashboards often do 20 panels; prefetch could increase memory & fanout.

oliver: yep. two mitigations: batching prefetches per dashboard load and adaptive fanout (start with top-k visible panels). also use prefix/KV reuse: many panels reuse the same timeseries queries.

lina: ops question: cache invalidation when policy changes. if policy-version in token is stale, we must reject tokens. how expensive is a global policy bump?

oliver: tokens carry policy-version + a policy-epoch TTL. on policy change we increment policy-version; prefetch will be rejected and UI will force-refresh. we won't try to invalidate every cache entry synchronously. this keeps complexity low but means short window of stale tokens (configurable, minutes).

sam: ok but what about audit logs? we need per-tenant authz decisions logged for compliance. prefetch centralizes checks — audit must record prefetch verdict + token id.

jen: agree. also need tracing: link render spans back to prefetch span via token id.

kevin: rollout plan? feature flag? can we A/B by tenant?

oliver: propose layered rollout: start internal + staging tenants, then opt-in by percentage, finally default on new dashboards. Flag gating: ui sends header X-Use-Prefetch: true. server side honors flag per-tenant. metrics: per-panel tail latency, prefetch hit rate, token rejection rate, audit events.

lina: monitoring thresholds? if prefetch miss rate > 10% we should pause auto-rollout. Also SLI: p95 panel render < 150ms.

oliver: agreed. implementation notes: prefetch service will be colocated with query-layer to reuse cached DB results and avoid double fetch. renders run in a separate pool optimized with no auth libs.

sam: security nit: token should be signed+encrypted HMAC with key rotation via KMS. keep TTL short (30s-2m).

oliver: noted. we'll draft key rotation + reconciliation docs.

jen: does this affect analytics queries (heavy joins)? prefetch might spike query traffic if lots of dashboards refresh simultaneously.

kevin: consider request shaping & eviction: prefetch queue with concurrency limits + backpressure to UI (304/429). also use progressive hydration: first fetch summaries.

lina: ops follow-ups: 1) ability to flush prefetch caches per-tenant 2) dashboards to expose "force refresh" for on-call 3) rollout dashboard for monitoring.

oliver: will add to RFC follow-up doc. action items: @maya to prototype token shape + minimal cache, @sam to write KMS rotation plan, @jen to sketch rollout flagging, @kevin to propose throttling knobs, @lina to list monitoring dashboards.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled for canary namespace at 2024-12-10T03:00Z (dry run).

maya: I'll start a prototype PR tomorrow, will post link here.

jen: thanks — this is a nice way to get tail latency wins without major model change. :thumbsup:

kevin: one more: consider metrics for "render-only failures" where token valid but cache missing data -> degrade UI gracefully.

oliver: good call. add metric: token-valid-prefetch-miss_count. end.
